Apple___Apple_scab.description: A fungal disease that can affect apple leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Olive to brown leaf spots; infected leaves may drop early.
prevention: Choose resistant cultivars and manage fallen infected leaves.
Apple___Apple_scab.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Apple scab

Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease associated with leaf spots, fruit decay and cankers.
symptoms: Circular leaf spots with purple margins and tan centers.
prevention: Remove dead wood and mummified fruit; reduce tree stress.
Apple___Black_rot.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Black rot of apple

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A rust disease whose life cycle involves apple relatives and junipers.
symptoms: Yellow to orange spots on leaves.
prevention: Choose resistant apple varieties when establishing plantings.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Cedar-apple rust

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A fungal foliar disease of corn.
symptoms: Gray to brown rectangular lesions, often bounded by veins.
prevention: Use resistant hybrids and rotate crops.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Gray leaf spot on corn

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: A fungal rust disease of corn.
symptoms: Brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Common rust on corn

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: A fungal leaf blight of corn.
symptoms: Long canoe-shaped or cigar-shaped leaf lesions.
prevention: Use resistant hybrids and crop rotation.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Northern corn leaf blight

Potato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease affecting potato and tomato foliage.
symptoms: Brown leaf spots with concentric rings, often on older leaves.
prevention: Rotate crops and avoid wetting foliage when irrigating.
Potato___Early_blight.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Early blight in tomato and potato

Potato___Late_blight.description: A destructive disease of potato and tomato caused by Phytophthora infestans.
symptoms: Expanding water-soaked leaf lesions; pale growth may appear in humid conditions.
prevention: Use healthy planting material and scout for disease.
Potato___Late_blight.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Late blight

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease that can affect tomato foliage and fruit.
symptoms: Small dark leaf spots; early symptoms resemble other leaf-spot diseases.
prevention: Water at the plant base, improve airflow and avoid saving seed from infected plants.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Tomato leaf spot diseases

Tomato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease affecting tomato and potato.
symptoms: Brown leaf spots with concentric rings, often starting on older foliage.
prevention: Rotate crops, use healthy seed and avoid wetting foliage.
Tomato___Early_blight.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Early blight in tomato and potato

Tomato___Late_blight.description: A destructive disease caused by Phytophthora infestans.
symptoms: Water-soaked leaf lesions that expand rapidly in favorable wet conditions.
prevention: Use healthy transplants and scout regularly.
Tomato___Late_blight.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Late blight

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal foliar disease especially associated with greenhouse and high-tunnel tomatoes.
symptoms: Yellow areas above leaves with mold growth on the lower surface.
prevention: Improve ventilation, increase plant spacing and use drip irrigation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Tomato leaf mold

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A fungal leaf-spot disease of tomato.
symptoms: Small brown to dark leaf spots, commonly beginning on lower leaves.
prevention: Keep foliage dry during watering, improve airflow and mulch plants.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Tomato leaf spot diseases

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: Mite feeding damage is a pest condition rather than an infectious plant disease.
symptoms: Leaf stippling or discoloration and fine webbing.
prevention: Reduce plant water stress and conserve natural mite predators.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.source_title: University of California IPM: Spider mites

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: A fungal disease caused by Corynespora cassiicola.
symptoms: Small brown leaf spots that enlarge, sometimes with concentric rings.
prevention: Use healthy transplants, rotate with nonsolanaceous crops and remove plant debris.
Tomato___Target_Spot.source_title: University of Florida IFAS: Target Spot of Tomato in Florida (PP351)

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A viral disease spread by whiteflies and movement of infected plants.
symptoms: Small upward-curling yellow leaves and stunted growth.
prevention: Use resistant varieties and virus-free, whitefly-free transplants.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.source_title: University of California IPM: Tomato yellow leaf curl

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A viral condition requiring laboratory confirmation to distinguish it from similar disorders.
symptoms: Mottled light and dark leaf coloring, distortion and possible stunting.
prevention: Use disease-free seed or transplants and clean hands and tools.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.source_title: University of Minnesota Extension: Tomato viruses
